basis: Intellectual disability defines disease; amblyopia and bicuspid aortic valve each reported in 1/2 patients; small samples limit certainty. Mild clinodactyly alone does not establish damage.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis in 2/2 patients; secondary infections do not make this an immune disorder.
Constriction of the penile foreskin is a reproductive disorder; urinary tract damage is not intrinsic or established as common.
Definition identifies neurologic dysfunction, intestinal malformations/inflammation and combined immunodeficiency as the defining spectrum; their combinations vary across subtypes.
Neoplasm occupies the optic nerve, explicitly assigned to the ocular axis; CNS extension is not established as common.
Defined corneal stromal dystrophy; ocular primary applies despite the absence of visual impairment.
Congenital limb reduction with absence of forearm, wrist and hand.
Congenital skeletal malformation of the foot, supported by its dysostosis parent.
Meningeal tumour affecting the cerebral hemispheres.
Origin is paranasal sinus mucosal epithelium, within the pulmonary axis; the bone-carcinoma ancestor does not establish skeletal involvement.
Defined combined immunodeficiency; no additional organ damage is documented.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing impairment in 22/22 patients.
Premature fusion of cranial sutures defines the umbrella; additional organ disease varies by subtype.
Inborn GABA metabolic defect defined by obligate epileptic encephalopathy; cerebral dysmyelination and severe developmental delay occur in 80–99%.
Familial rhabdoid tumour syndrome defined by CNS and renal tumour sites; these primary labels describe its tumour spectrum, not damage in every mutation carrier.
Bladder carcinoma defines the primary site; advanced stage does not establish any particular additional organ as involved in at least 30%.
Hair and nail ectodermal dysplasia; sparse hair and dystrophic or absent nails define the affected tissues.
Autoimmune inflammation of the uvea; the erroneous ENT ancestry does not establish ear or airway disease.
Carcinoma arises from intrahepatic bile ducts, within the hepatic axis.
Posterior fossa cystic malformation, sometimes causing hydrocephalus; visual symptoms do not establish common lasting ocular damage.
Cardiomyopathy and hormonal gonadal failure define disease; ptosis and toe phalangeal aplasia each annotated at 80–99%; contractures/dislocation also reported. Neurologic findings are <30%.
Radiation-induced damage to brachial or lumbosacral peripheral nerve plexuses; treatment causation defines this disease itself.
Opioid toxicity is defined by CNS depression and suppression of ventilation; no additional organ damage is established as common.
Defining myopathy and skeletal deformities with cardiac disease; mitral regurgitation and ventricular hypertrophy each in 2/3. Transaminases alone do not establish liver damage.
Sex reversal and structural gonadal dysgenesis define this reproductive developmental disorder; hormonal failure is not documented. No evidence supports the cardiomyopathy ancestor.
